import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_55/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_55/training_1.csv"

df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation: JOIN on ["movieId", "movieId"] between Source2_55_0 and Source2_55_1
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1, on="movieId", how="inner")

# Select and cast columns to match target schema:
# Target Schema: ['movieId': integer, 'title': string, 'genres': string, 'userId': float, 'rating': float]

# movieId: integer
df_joined["movieId"] = df_joined["movieId"].astype(int)

# title: string (already string)
df_joined["title"] = df_joined["title"].astype(str)

# genres: string (already string)
df_joined["genres"] = df_joined["genres"].astype(str)

# userId: float (source is integer, convert to float)
df_joined["userId"] = df_joined["userId"].astype(float)

# rating: float (already float)
df_joined["rating"] = df_joined["rating"].astype(float)

# Construct final dataframe with columns in target schema order
df_target = df_joined[["movieId", "title", "genres", "userId", "rating"]]

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_55/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_55/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_55/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on movieId
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="movieId", how="inner")

# Group by movieId, title, genres, userId and aggregate rating by average
result = joined.groupby(["movieId", "title", "genres", "userId"], as_index=False).agg({"rating": "mean"})

# Ensure column order and types match target schema
result = result[["movieId", "title", "genres", "userId", "rating"]]
result["movieId"] = result["movieId"].astype(int)
result["userId"] = result["userId"].astype(float)
result["rating"] = result["rating"].astype(float)

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_55/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
